sanskrit: śubhaiḥ karmaphalair devi mayaite parikīrtitāḥ svargamārgopagā bhūyaḥ kim anyac chrotum icchasi
english: By the fruits of their good deeds, O goddess, these have been proclaimed by me as travellers upon the road to heaven. What else do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: umovāca mahān me saṃśayaḥ kaś cin martyān prati maheśvara tasmāt taṃ naipuṇenādya mamākhyātuṃ tvam arhasi
english: Umā said: A great doubt of mine concerns mortals, O Maheśvara; therefore it behoves you to expound it to me today with precision.

sanskrit: kenāyur labhate dīrghaṃ karmaṇā puruṣaḥ prabho tapasā vāpi deveśa kenāyur labhate mahat
english: By what deed does a man obtain long life, O Lord? By what austerity, O Lord of the gods, does he obtain a great span of years?

sanskrit: kṣīṇāyuḥ kena bhavati karmaṇā bhuvi mānavaḥ vipākaṃ karmaṇāṃ deva vaktum arhasy anindita
english: By what deed does a man on earth become short-lived? Be pleased to declare the ripening of deeds, O blameless god.

sanskrit: apare ca mahābhogā mandabhogās tathāpare akulīnās tathā cānye kulīnāś ca tathāpare
english: Some men enjoy great wealth, while others enjoy but little; some are of low birth, and yet others are of noble birth.

sanskrit: durdarśāḥ ke cid ābhānti narāḥ kāṣṭhamayā iva priyadarśās tathā cānye darśanād eva mānavāḥ
english: Some men appear ill-favoured to look upon, as though carved of wood, while other men are pleasing at the very first sight.

sanskrit: duṣprajñāḥ ke cid ābhānti ke cid ābhānti paṇḍitāḥ mahāprajñās tathaivānye jñānavijñānadarśinaḥ
english: Some appear dull of wit, some appear learned, and others again are of great wisdom, perceivers of knowledge and discernment.

sanskrit: alpābādhās tathā ke cin mahābādhās tathāpare dṛśyante puruṣā deva tan me śaṃsitum arhasi
english: Some men are seen to suffer little affliction and others great affliction, O god; it behoves you to explain this to me.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca hanta te 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi devi karmaphalodayam martyaloke narāḥ sarve yena svaṃ bhuñjate phalam
english: Maheśvara said: Come then, I shall declare to you, O goddess, the arising of the fruit of deeds, whereby all men in the world of mortals reap each his own reward.

sanskrit: prāṇātipātī yo raudro daṇḍahastodyatas tathā nityam udyatadaṇḍaś ca hanti bhūtagaṇān naraḥ
english: The man who is a slayer of living things, cruel, ever with rod uplifted in hand, and ever ready to strike, who kills the hosts of creatures—

sanskrit: nirdayaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ nityam udvegakārakaḥ api kīṭapipīlānām aśaraṇyaḥ sunirghṛṇaḥ
english: merciless toward all beings, ever a maker of terror, offering no refuge even to worms and ants, utterly without pity—

sanskrit: evaṃbhūto naro devi nirayaṃ pratipadyate viparītas tu dharmātmā rūpavān abhijāyate
english: such a man, O goddess, comes to hell; but his opposite, the righteous-souled, is born handsome of form.

sanskrit: nirayaṃ yāti hiṃsātmā yāti svargam ahiṃsakaḥ yātanāṃ niraye raudrāṃ sa kṛcchrāṃ labhate naraḥ
english: The cruel-souled goes to hell, the harmless goes to heaven; and in hell that man obtains fierce and grievous torment.

sanskrit: atha cen nirayāt tasmāt samuttarati karhi cit mānuṣyaṃ labhate cāpi hīnāyus tatra jāyate
english: And if at length he rises up out of that hell and obtains human birth, even then he is born there short-lived.

sanskrit: pāpena karmaṇā devi baddho hiṃsāratir naraḥ apriyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hīnāyur upajāyate
english: Bound by his sinful deed, O goddess, the man who delighted in violence is born hateful to all beings and short of life.

sanskrit: yas tu śuklābhijātīyaḥ prāṇighātavivarjakaḥ nikṣiptadaṇḍo nirdaṇḍo na hinasti kadā cana
english: But he who is of pure nature, abstaining from the slaying of living things, who has laid down the rod and bears no rod, who never does harm—

sanskrit: na ghātayati no hanti ghnantaṃ naivānumodate sarvabhūteṣu sasneho yathātmani tathāpare
english: who neither causes slaughter nor slays, nor approves of one who slays, but is loving toward all beings, regarding others as he regards himself—

sanskrit: īdṛśaḥ puruṣotkarṣo devi devatvam aśnute upapannān sukhān bhogān upāśnāti mudā yutaḥ
english: such an excellent man, O goddess, attains to godhood, and joyfully enjoys the happy delights that fall to his lot.

sanskrit: atha cen mānuṣe loke kadā cid upapadyate tatra dīrghāyur utpannaḥ sa naraḥ sukham edhate
english: And if at some time he is reborn in the world of men, that man, born long-lived, flourishes there in happiness.

sanskrit: evaṃ dīrghāyuṣāṃ mārgaḥ suvṛttānāṃ sukarmaṇām prāṇihiṃsāvimokṣeṇa brahmaṇā samudīritaḥ
english: Thus the path of the long-lived, of those of good conduct and good deeds, lies through the renunciation of harm to living things—so it was declared by Brahmā.

sanskrit: umovāca kiṃśīlāḥ kiṃsamācārāḥ puruṣāḥ kaiś ca karmabhiḥ svargaṃ samabhipadyante saṃpradānena kena vā
english: Umā said: Of what character, of what conduct, and by what deeds do men attain to heaven, and by what kind of giving?

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca dātā brāhmaṇasatkartā dīnāndhakṛpaṇādiṣu bhakṣyabhojyānnapānānāṃ vāsasāṃ ca pradāyakaḥ
english: Maheśvara said: The giver, the honourer of brāhmaṇas, the bestower of foods to be chewed and eaten, of grain, of drink, and of garments upon the poor, the blind, the wretched, and the like—

sanskrit: pratiśrayān sabhāḥ kūpān prapāḥ puṣkariṇīs tathā naityakāni ca sarvāṇi kim icchakam atīva ca
english: who gives shelters, assembly-halls, wells, watering-stations, and lotus-pools, and all the daily necessaries, and abundantly whatever is desired—

sanskrit: āsanaṃ śayanaṃ yānaṃ dhanaṃ ratnaṃ gṛhāṃs tathā sasyajātāni sarvāṇi gāḥ kṣetrāṇy atha yoṣitaḥ
english: seats, beds, vehicles, wealth, jewels, and houses, all kinds of crops, cattle, fields, and even women—

sanskrit: supratītamanā nityaṃ yaḥ prayacchati mānavaḥ evaṃbhūto mṛto devi devaloke 'bhijāyate
english: the man who gives these ever with a glad and trusting heart—such a one, O goddess, when he dies is born in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: tatroṣya suciraṃ kālaṃ bhuktvā bhogān anuttamān sahāpsarobhir mudito ramitvā nandanādiṣu
english: Dwelling there a very long time, enjoying delights unsurpassed, rejoicing and sporting with the apsarases in Nandana and the other groves,

sanskrit: tasmāt svargāc cyuto lokān mānuṣeṣūpajāyate mahābhoge kule devi dhanadhānyasamācite
english: and fallen from that heaven, he is reborn among the worlds of men, O goddess, in a family of great wealth, well furnished with riches and grain.

sanskrit: tatra kāmaguṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ samupeto mudā yutaḥ mahābhogo mahākośo dhanī bhavati mānavaḥ
english: There, endowed with every quality that the heart desires and filled with joy, the man becomes one of great enjoyment, of great treasure, and rich.

sanskrit: ete devi mahābhogāḥ prāṇino dānaśīlinaḥ brahmaṇā vai purā proktāḥ sarvasya priyadarśanāḥ
english: These beings of great enjoyment, O goddess, given to charity, were declared of old by Brahmā to be pleasing to the sight of all.

sanskrit: apare mānavā devi pradānakṛpaṇā dvijaiḥ yācitā na prayacchanti vidyamāne 'py abuddhayaḥ
english: Other men, O goddess, are miserly in giving, and though they possess the means, when entreated by the twice-born they do not give, being foolish.

sanskrit: dīnāndhakṛpaṇān dṛṣṭvā bhikṣukān atithīn api yācyamānā nivartante jihvālobhasamanvitāḥ
english: Seeing the poor, the blind, the wretched, beggars, and even guests entreating them, they turn away, possessed by greed of the palate.

sanskrit: na dhanāni na vāsāṃsi na bhogān na ca kāñcanam na gāvo nānnavikṛtiṃ prayacchanti kadā cana
english: Neither wealth nor garments nor enjoyments nor gold, neither cattle nor any dish of food do they ever give.

sanskrit: apravṛttās tu ye lubdhā nāstikā dānavarjitāḥ evaṃbhūtā narā devi nirayaṃ yānty abuddhayaḥ
english: Those who are inactive in good, greedy, unbelieving, and devoid of charity—such men, O goddess, the foolish, go to hell.

sanskrit: te cen manuṣyatāṃ yānti yadā kālasya paryayāt dhanarikte kule janma labhante svalpabuddhayaḥ
english: And if in the course of time they come again to human birth, those of little understanding obtain birth in a family empty of wealth.

sanskrit: kṣutpipāsāparītāś ca sarvabhogabahiṣkṛtāḥ nirāśāḥ sarvabhogebhyo jīvanty adhamajīvikām
english: Beset by hunger and thirst, cast out from all enjoyments, hopeless of every pleasure, they live the meanest of lives.

sanskrit: alpabhogakule jātā alpabhogaratā narāḥ anena karmaṇā devi bhavanty adhanino narāḥ
english: Born in a family of meagre means, men content with meagre enjoyments—by this deed, O goddess, men become destitute of wealth.

sanskrit: apare stambhino nityaṃ māninaḥ pāpato ratāḥ āsanārhasya ye pīṭhaṃ na prayacchanty acetasaḥ
english: Others, ever stiff with pride, vain, delighting in sin, the senseless who do not offer a seat to one who deserves a seat—

sanskrit: mārgārhasya ca ye mārgaṃ na yacchanty alpabuddhayaḥ pādyārhasya ca ye pādyaṃ na dadaty alpabuddhayaḥ
english: who, of little wit, do not yield the way to one who deserves the way, and who, of little wit, do not offer water for the feet to one who deserves it—

sanskrit: arghārhān na ca satkārair arcayanti yathāvidhi arghyam ācamanīyaṃ vā na yacchanty alpabuddhayaḥ
english: who do not honour with due rites those worthy of honour, and who, of little wit, do not offer the welcome-offering or water for rinsing the mouth—

sanskrit: guruṃ cābhigataṃ premṇā guruvan na bubhūṣate abhimānapravṛttena lobhena samavasthitāḥ
english: who do not wish to honour as a teacher the teacher come in love, but are settled in greed driven by arrogance—

sanskrit: saṃmānyāṃś cāvamanyante vṛddhān paribhavanti ca evaṃvidhā narā devi sarve nirayagāminaḥ
english: who slight those worthy of respect and despise their elders—such men, O goddess, all go to hell.

sanskrit: te vai yadi narās tasmān nirayād uttaranti vai varṣapūgais tato janma labhante kutsite kule
english: And if those men rise up at last from that hell, then after a long succession of years they obtain birth in a despised family.

sanskrit: śvapākapulkasādīnāṃ kutsitānām acetasām kuleṣu teṣu jāyante guruvṛddhāpacāyinaḥ
english: In the families of the despised and senseless—dog-cookers, pulkasas, and the like—are born those who had slighted their teachers and elders.

sanskrit: na stambhī na ca mānī yo devatādvijapūjakaḥ lokapūjyo namaskartā praśrito madhuraṃ vadan
english: He who is neither stiff with pride nor vain, a worshipper of gods and brāhmaṇas, honoured by the world, a maker of reverence, modest, sweet of speech,

sanskrit: sarvavarṇapriyakaraḥ sarvabhūtahitaḥ sadā adveṣī sumukhaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ snigdhavāṇīpradaḥ sadā
english: who does what is pleasing to all the varṇas, ever intent on the welfare of all beings, free from malice, of pleasant countenance, gentle, ever uttering affectionate words,

sanskrit: svāgatenaiva sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām avihiṃsakaḥ yathārhasatkriyāpūrvam arcayann upatiṣṭhati
english: who harms no being and greets all with welcome, and who waits upon them, honouring each with the courtesy he deserves,

sanskrit: mārgārhāya dadan mārgaṃ guruṃ guruvad arcayan atithipragraharatas tathābhyāgatapūjakaḥ
english: yielding the way to one who deserves the way, honouring the teacher as a teacher, delighting to receive guests, and a worshipper of those who come—

sanskrit: evaṃbhūto naro devi svargatiṃ pratipadyate tato mānuṣatāṃ prāpya viśiṣṭakulajo bhavet
english: such a man, O goddess, attains to heaven, and thereafter, gaining human birth, is born in a distinguished family.

sanskrit: tatrāsau vipulair bhogaiḥ sarvaratnasamāyutaḥ yathārhadātā cārheṣu dharmacaryāparo bhavet
english: There, possessed of ample enjoyments and furnished with every jewel, he becomes a giver to the worthy according to their deserts and devoted to the practice of dharma.

sanskrit: saṃmataḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ svakarmaphalam āpnoti svayam eva naraḥ sadā
english: Esteemed by all beings and honoured by all the world, the man himself ever obtains the fruit of his own deeds.

sanskrit: udāttakulajātīya udāttābhijanaḥ sadā eṣa dharmo mayā prokto vidhātrā svayam īritaḥ
english: Born of an exalted family and ever of exalted lineage—this is the law I have declared, the very law set forth by the Ordainer himself.

sanskrit: yas tu raudrasamācāraḥ sarvasattvabhayaṃkaraḥ hastābhyāṃ yadi vā padbhyāṃ rajjvā daṇḍena vā punaḥ
english: But he who is of cruel conduct, a terror to all creatures, who with his hands or his feet, or again with rope or rod,

sanskrit: loṣṭaiḥ stambhair upāyair vā jantūn bādhati śobhane hiṃsārthaṃ nikṛtiprajñaḥ prodvejayati caiva ha
english: with clods or posts or by other devices torments living beings, O lovely one—who, with a mind bent on cunning and cruelty, terrifies them,

sanskrit: upakrāmati jantūṃś ca udvegajananaḥ sadā evaṃśīlasamācāro nirayaṃ pratipadyate
english: and assails creatures, ever a maker of terror—such a one, of such character and conduct, comes to hell.

sanskrit: sa cen mānuṣatāṃ gacched yadi kālasya paryayāt bahvābādhaparikliṣṭe so 'dhame jāyate kule
english: And if in the course of time he should come to human birth, he is born in a low family, sorely afflicted with many ailments.

sanskrit: lokadveṣyo 'dhamaḥ puṃsāṃ svayaṃ karmakṛtaiḥ phalaiḥ eṣa devi manuṣyeṣu boddhavyo jñātibandhuṣu
english: Hated by the world, the lowest of men through the fruits wrought by his own deeds—this, O goddess, is to be understood among men and among kinsmen and relations.

sanskrit: aparaḥ sarvabhūtāni dayāvān anupaśyati maitradṛṣṭiḥ pitṛsamo nirvairo niyatendriyaḥ
english: Another, full of compassion, looks upon all beings with a friendly eye, like a father, free from enmity, with senses restrained;

sanskrit: nodvejayati bhūtāni na vihiṃsayate tathā hastapādaiḥ suniyatair viśvāsyaḥ sarvajantuṣu
english: he neither frightens beings nor does them harm, and with hands and feet well controlled he is trusted among all creatures.

sanskrit: na rajjvā na ca daṇḍena na loṣṭair nāyudhena ca udvejayati bhūtāni ślakṣṇakarmā dayāparaḥ
english: Neither with rope nor with rod, nor with clods nor with weapon does he terrify beings—gentle in his deeds and given to compassion.

sanskrit: evaṃśīlasamācāraḥ svarge samupajāyate tatrāsau bhavane divye mudā vasati devavat
english: One of such character and conduct is born in heaven, and there in a divine mansion he dwells in joy, like a god.

sanskrit: sa cet karmakṣayān martyo manuṣyeṣūpajāyate alpābādho nirītīkaḥ sa jātaḥ sukham edhate
english: And if, when his merit is spent, the mortal is reborn among men, he, born free from ailment and from calamity, flourishes in happiness.

sanskrit: sukhabhāgī nirāyāso nirudvegaḥ sadā naraḥ eṣa devi satāṃ mārgo bādhā yatra na vidyate
english: A partaker of happiness, untoiling, and ever free from agitation is that man. This, O goddess, is the path of the good, where no affliction is found.

sanskrit: umovāca ime manuṣyā dṛśyante ūhāpohaviśāradāḥ jñānavijñānasaṃpannāḥ prajñāvanto 'rthakovidāḥ duṣprajñāś cāpare deva jñānavijñānavarjitāḥ
english: Umā said: These men are seen skilled in reasoning for and against, endowed with knowledge and discernment, wise and versed in affairs; while others, O god, are dull of wit, devoid of knowledge and discernment.

sanskrit: kena karmavipākena prajñāvān puruṣo bhavet alpaprajño virūpākṣa kathaṃ bhavati mānavaḥ etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ chinddhi sarvadharmavidāṃ vara
english: By the ripening of what deed does a man become wise? How does a man come to be of little wisdom, O three-eyed one? Cut away this doubt of mine, O best of all who know dharma.

sanskrit: jātyandhāś cāpare deva rogārtāś cāpare tathā narāḥ klībāś ca dṛśyante kāraṇaṃ brūhi tatra vai
english: And some men, O god, are seen blind from birth, others afflicted with disease, and others impotent; tell me the cause therein.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca brāhmaṇān vedaviduṣaḥ siddhān dharmavidas tathā paripṛcchanty aharahaḥ kuśalākuśalaṃ tathā
english: Maheśvara said: Those who day by day inquire of brāhmaṇas learned in the Vedas, of the perfected, and of those who know dharma, concerning what is right and wrong,

sanskrit: varjayanty aśubhaṃ karma sevamānāḥ śubhaṃ tathā labhante svargatiṃ nityam iha loke sukhaṃ tathā
english: who shun the unwholesome deed and cleave to the wholesome, ever obtain heaven and happiness here in this world.

sanskrit: sa cen mānuṣatāṃ yāti medhāvī tatra jāyate śrutaṃ prajñānugaṃ cāsya kalyāṇam upajāyate
english: And if such a one comes to human birth, he is born there of keen intellect, and learning, attended by wisdom and blessedness, arises in him.

sanskrit: paradāreṣu ye mūḍhāś cakṣur duṣṭaṃ prayuñjate tena duṣṭasvabhāvena jātyandhās te bhavanti ha
english: Those fools who cast a wicked eye upon the wives of others—by that wicked disposition they become blind from birth.

sanskrit: manasā tu praduṣṭena nagnāṃ paśyanti ye striyam rogārtās te bhavantīha narā duṣkṛtakarmiṇaḥ
english: And those who with corrupted mind gaze upon a naked woman—such men, doers of evil deeds, become afflicted with disease here.

sanskrit: ye tu mūḍhā durācārā viyonau maithune ratāḥ puruṣeṣu suduṣprajñāḥ klībatvam upayānti te
english: But those deluded, ill-conducted, very foolish men who delight in unnatural intercourse with men come to impotence.

sanskrit: paśūṃś ca ye bandhayanti ye caiva gurutalpagāḥ prakīrṇamaithunā ye ca klībā jāyanti te narāḥ
english: Those who couple beasts, those who defile the bed of their teacher, and those of promiscuous intercourse—such men are born impotent.

sanskrit: umovāca sāvadyaṃ kiṃ nu vai karma niravadyaṃ tathaiva ca śreyaḥ kurvann avāpnoti mānavo devasattama
english: Umā said: What deed is blameworthy, and what is blameless, and what is the higher good that a man obtains by doing it, O best of the gods?

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca śreyāṃsaṃ mārgam ātiṣṭhan sadā yaḥ pṛcchate dvijān dharmānveṣī guṇākāṅkṣī sa svargaṃ samupāśnute
english: Maheśvara said: He who, keeping ever to the better path, inquires of the twice-born, a seeker of dharma and a yearner after virtue, attains to heaven.

sanskrit: yadi mānuṣatāṃ devi kadā cit sa nigacchati medhāvī dhāraṇāyuktaḥ prājñas tatrābhijāyate
english: And if at some time, O goddess, he comes to human birth, he is born there of keen intellect, endowed with retentive memory, and wise.

sanskrit: eṣa devi satāṃ dharmo mantavyo bhūtikārakaḥ nṛṇāṃ hitārthāya tava mayā vai samudāhṛtaḥ
english: This, O goddess, is the law of the good, to be deemed a maker of prosperity; for the welfare of men it has been declared by me to you.

sanskrit: umovāca apare svalpavijñānā dharmavidveṣiṇo narāḥ brāhmaṇān vedaviduṣo necchanti parisarpitum
english: Umā said: Other men, of scant understanding and haters of dharma, do not wish to wait attentively upon brāhmaṇas learned in the Vedas.

sanskrit: vratavanto narāḥ ke cic chraddhādamaparāyaṇāḥ avratā bhraṣṭaniyamās tathānye rākṣasopamāḥ
english: Some men hold to vows, devoted to faith and self-restraint; others are without vows, fallen from the rules, and like rākṣasas.

sanskrit: yajvānaś ca tathaivānye nirhomāś ca tathāpare kena karmavipākena bhavantīha vadasva me
english: Some, again, are performers of sacrifice, and others offer no oblations; by the ripening of what deed do they become so here? Tell me.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca āgamāl lokadharmāṇāṃ maryādāḥ pūrvanirmitāḥ prāmāṇyenānuvartante dṛśyante hi dṛḍhavratāḥ
english: Maheśvara said: From the tradition of the laws of the world, the bounds were established of old; through their authority men follow them, and so the firm in vows are seen.
